canonical_name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
metric: accuracy (% of prompts / instructions whose verifiable constraints are satisfied; 4 variants: prompt-level strict [headline], instruction-level strict, prompt-level loose, instruction-level loose)
n_items_source: arXiv 2311.07911v1 (541 prompts, 25 verifiable instruction types); data in google-research/instruction_following_eval
score_at_release_setting: zero-shot; prompt-level strict accuracy. Same model: instruction-level strict 83.57, prompt-level loose 79.30, instruction-level loose 85.37. Only other model: PaLM 2 S 43.07 / 55.76 / 46.95 / 59.11
human_source: No human baseline reported in v1
test_access_notes: All prompts and the deterministic checker code are public (google-research/google-research/tree/master/instruction_following_eval); no hidden labels (grading is programmatic).
curation_notes: 4 steps: base prompts generated with 1-3 randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; few-shot LLM prompting to remove illogical prompts; few-shot LLM rephrasing for diversity; then manual check/edit of each prompt.
maintainer: Google (Google Research; one Yale co-author)
official_leaderboard: no (no official leaderboard; later adopted e.g. by Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard v2)
lineage: No parent. Derivatives/successors: Multi-IF (Meta, Oct 2024, multi-turn/multilingual), M-IFEval (multilingual, Feb 2025, arXiv 2502.04688), IFBench (AI2, Jul 2025, arXiv 2507.02833, new out-of-domain constraints), IFEval++ (Dec 2025, arXiv 2512.14754).
known_contamination_or_defects: IFBench paper (arXiv 2507.02833) reports models 'strongly overfit' to the small set of verifiable constraint types in benchmarks such as IFEval (constraint-targeted post-training data). IFEval++ (arXiv 2512.14754) re-checked original IFEval prompts and found 'many flagged cases were indeed flawed or ambiguous' and corrected them (no count given). No formal label-error audit found.
notes: Format: free-form responses graded by deterministic Python verifiers (no LLM judge). Headline metric in most later reports is prompt-level strict (some report the mean of the 4 variants). v1 submitted 14 Nov 2023.

canonical_name: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
metric: accuracy (quasi-exact match of final answer vs. ground truth, normalised by answer type); reported per level (1-3) and overall
n_items_source: Paper v1: 466 questions = 166 annotated dev/validation + 300 test with withheld answers (Level 1/2/3 = 146/245/75 overall). Released HF splits (inferred from official results_public denominators): test 301 (L1 93 / L2 159 / L3 49), validation 165 (L1 53 / L2 86 / L3 26). Many agent papers report on the public 165-question validation split.
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 + manually selected plugins (oracle setting, authors' baseline)
score_at_release_setting: Abstract headline: 'humans 92% vs. 15% for GPT-4 equipped with plugins'. Table 4 per level: L1 30.3 / L2 9.7 / L3 0 (plugins chosen manually per question; flagged as not reproducible). Other paper baselines (L1/L2/L3): GPT-4 9.1/2.6/0; GPT-4 Turbo 13.0/5.5/0; AutoGPT-4 14.4/0.4/0; search engine 7.4/0/0. Official HF test leaderboard at launch held only authors' baselines: GPT-4 Turbo 6.64 (20/301), AutoGPT4 4.98, GPT-4 3.99, GPT-3.5 2.66.
n_annotators: 2 independent validators per question (Surge AI paid annotators + authors' teams); total head-count not reported
human_source: arXiv 2311.12983v1: 'annotator success rate 92% aggregated on all levels' (L1 93.9 / L2 91.8 / L3 87.3); = share of correct answers by validation annotators on valid questions
test_access_notes: Questions public; answers to the test split withheld and scored on the Hugging Face leaderboard; validation split (165) released with answers (gated HF dataset).
curation_notes: Questions written and validated by paid annotators (Surge AI) together with the authors' teams; designed to have unambiguous short answers requiring web browsing, multimodality, tool use and file handling.
maintainer: Meta (GenAI/FAIR) + Hugging Face (with AutoGPT co-authors)
lineage: GAIA (Nov 2023) -> Gaia2 within Meta ARE 'Agents Research Environments' (Sep 2025, arXiv 2509.17158).
known_contamination_or_defects: Independent audit 'gaia-verified' (Jul 2026, https://github.com/anirudhvenu/gaia-verified): 27 of 165 validation tasks (16.4%) mis-scored (10 source drift, 8 question/answer mismatch, 6 annotator error, 2 format, 1 multiple correct answers). Validation answers are public, so validation-split scores are contamination-prone.
notes: Agentic: questions require web browsing/tool use; attachments include images, spreadsheets, audio, etc. (hence multimodal-other). Paper's split of Table 4 (dev vs test) is not stated explicitly. Human time per question 6-17 min by level.

canonical_name: MMMU: Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning benchmark
metric: accuracy (micro-averaged, zero-shot)
n_items_source: arXiv 2311.16502v1: 11,550 questions, dev:val:test = 150:900:10,500. De-facto standard for model reports is the 900-question validation split.
score_at_release_setting: zero-shot; validation split (900). Same model on test (10,500): 55.7. Best open-source in v1: LLaVA-1.5-13B 36.4 val / 33.6 test; BLIP-2 FLAN-T5-XXL 35.4 val / 34.0 test. Text-only GPT-4: 34.9 val / 33.8 test; random 22.1 val / 23.9 test. (Gemini Ultra 59.4 val added in later versions after 6 Dec 2023.)
human_source: Added after v1 (leaderboard news 2024-01-31; arXiv v4 Table 2): Expert worst 76.2 / medium 82.6 / best 88.6 on the 900 validation questions; open-book (textbooks allowed, no Internet). Not in v1.
test_access_notes: Test answers withheld; EvalAI evaluation server from 2023-12-04. Website news 2026-02-12: test-set answers released publicly (now public). Dev/val answers public from the start.
curation_notes: Collected from college exams, quizzes and textbooks by >50 university students (incl. co-authors); some questions created by annotators; annotators told to prefer questions without readily available answers.
maintainer: MMMU team (Xiang Yue, Wenhu Chen, Yu Su et al.; IN.AI Research, Univ. of Waterloo, Ohio State Univ. and others)
lineage: MMMU (Nov 2023) -> MMMU-Pro (Sep 2024, arXiv 2409.02813); language/modality variants CMMMU (Chinese, Jan 2024), JMMMU (Japanese, 2024), Video-MMMU (2025).
known_contamination_or_defects: MMMU-Pro (arXiv 2409.02813) showed a substantial share of MMMU questions are answerable by text-only LLMs and filtered them (see MMMU-Pro row). Test answers released Feb 2026 (hidden test no longer hidden). No formal label-error audit found.
notes: 94.03% multiple-choice (10,861), 5.97% open short-answer (689); 30 subjects, 183 subfields, 30 image types. v1 submitted 27 Nov 2023.

canonical_name: GPQA (Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A) - Diamond subset
metric: accuracy (4-option multiple choice)
n_items_source: arXiv 2311.12022v1 Table 2: Extended 546, Main 448, Diamond 198
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 (few-shot CoT); GPT-4 with search also 38.8
score_at_release_setting: few-shot chain-of-thought, Diamond set. Other Diamond baselines: GPT-3.5-turbo few-shot CoT 29.6; Llama-2-70B few-shot CoT 28.1. GPT-4 few-shot CoT on Main 39.7 / Extended 38.7.
n_annotators: 61 Upwork contractors in total (writers + validators); per question 2 expert validators + 3 non-expert validators
human_source: arXiv v1 Table 2: expert validator accuracy on Diamond 81.3 (flagged as skewed upward by selection effects); non-expert validators (skilled, web access, ~30 min) 22.1. Main: 71.9 / 30.4; Extended: 64.8 / 34.1.
test_access_notes: Full dataset released (password-protected zip with canary string; authors ask not to reveal examples in plain text online). No hidden test.
curation_notes: Questions written by PhD-level domain experts (biology, physics, chemistry) hired via Upwork; validated by other experts and 'Google-proofed' against skilled non-experts with web access. Diamond = questions where both experts answer correctly (or the 2nd expert's error is clearly acknowledged) and the majority of non-experts answer incorrectly.
maintainer: NYU (David Rein, Samuel R. Bowman et al.; co-authors also from Cohere and Anthropic)
lineage: GPQA Extended (546) > Main (448) > Diamond (198), all released Nov 2023. No official successor version; later 'harder science QA' benchmarks (e.g., SuperGPQA 2025, Humanity's Last Exam 2025) are by other teams.
known_contamination_or_defects: Label noise: D. Rein (NYU ARG blog, May 2024, https://wp.nyu.edu/arg/can-good-benchmarks-contain-mistakes/) - up to ~1/3 of Extended questions may contain mistakes; true fraction of objectively correct Diamond questions 'likely between 74% and 100%'. Epoch AI (G. Burnham, May 2025, https://epoch.ai/gradient-updates/gpqa-diamond-whats-left): rough estimate ~8% (15/198) invalid, '>=90% valid'. Contamination mitigations: canary string, encrypted release.
notes: Diamond is the de-facto standard subset in model reports. Human expert number on Diamond is inflated by construction (selection on expert agreement).

canonical_name: MERA: Multimodal Evaluation for Russian-language Architectures (text benchmark, v1.0)
metric: Total score = mean of per-task scores (accuracy, F1/EM, MCC, pass@k, normalised exam grade) over the 17 non-diagnostic tasks; 4 diagnostic tasks excluded
n_items_source: Derived: sum of per-task test sizes in arXiv 2401.04531v1 Table 1 for the 17 scored tasks (16,561; 19,739 incl. 4 diagnostic tasks); 21 tasks total at v1.0; ruModAr alone has 6,000 test items.
score_at_release_setting: Authors' baselines of open models via MERA's lm-evaluation-harness fork (prompts and few-shot/zero-shot settings fixed per task). Others: Llama-2-13b 28.4, Yi-6B 28.4, Llama-2-7b 27.6, ruGPT-3.5 20.4; random baseline 20.5.
n_annotators: overlap 5 per example before filtering, majority vote; total head-count not reported
human_source: arXiv 2401.04531v1: human baseline via Toloka and ABC Elementary crowdsourcing (paid training/exam/main stages), final answer by majority vote; Total 87.2
test_access_notes: Test answers held only by organizers; participants run models on test inputs and upload predictions to mera.a-ai.ru for closed automatic scoring.
curation_notes: Some tasks created from scratch for MERA; others converted/adapted from Russian SuperGLUE, TAPE and translated English datasets (e.g., ruMMLU, ruHumanEval, ruHHH, ruOpenBookQA); exam-based tasks (USE = Russian Unified State Exam, CheGeKa quiz game).
maintainer: AI Alliance Russia: SberDevices, Sber AI, HSE University, Skoltech, AIRI and others
lineage: Builds on Russian SuperGLUE (2020) and TAPE (2022). MERA v1.0.0 (Nov 2023, 21 tasks) -> v1.1.0 (2024; arXiv v3/ACL 2024 camera-ready aligned with it) -> v1.2.0 (Sept 2024; improved prompts/datasets, dynamic leaderboard; README now lists 23 text tasks) -> sibling tracks MERA Industrial (2025), MERA Code (2025), SWE-MERA (2025), MERA Multi (multimodal, 2025).
known_contamination_or_defects: No formal label-error/contamination audit found. Several tasks derive from public datasets (translations of MMLU/HumanEval etc.), whose answers exist online.
notes: Announced at Sber's AI Journey (Nov 2023); arXiv v1 9 Jan 2024. First external measurement round announced 6 Feb 2024 (>20 models; GigaChat Pro led, score not stated). Format mixed: multiple-choice/classification, free-form EM/F1, code pass@k, exam grading. Score scale 0-100 in paper vs 0-1 on site.

canonical_name: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
metric: attack success rate (ASR, %) = share of test cases whose completion the HarmBench classifier judges as exhibiting the harmful behavior; computed per (attack x target model). Direction: lower ASR = more robust model; higher = stronger attack
n_items_source: Paper: 510 behaviors (400 textual = 200 standard + 100 contextual + 100 copyright; 110 multimodal); official split validation 100 (40 standard/20 contextual/20 copyright/20 multimodal) / test 410 -> textual test = 320 (160/80/80) + 90 multimodal (derived from stated val composition).
score_at_release_system: Claude 2.1 (most robust target model; defense view)
score_at_release_setting: DERIVED: mean ASR over the 8 attacks run on closed models, test text behaviors (Table 8): GCG-Transfer 2.9, Zero-Shot 3.9, PAIR 2.2, TAP 2.5, TAP-Transfer 0.6, PAP-top5 1.1, Human jailbreaks 0.2, DirectRequest 1.9 (Claude 2: mean 2.0). Attack view (paper ranks attacks by 'Average (up)' ASR across models): GCG 54.2 (white-box, open models only), AutoDAN 52.8, TAP-T 48.7. Authors' adversarially trained Zephyr-7B+R2D2: GCG ASR 6.3 vs 69.4 for Zephyr 7B. GPT-4 Turbo 1106: up to 57.7 (TAP-T).
score_at_release_source: Table 8 'Attack Success Rate on HarmBench - Test Behaviors' in the ICML 2024 version (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/mazeika24a.html); arXiv v1 (6 Feb 2024) appendix tables could not be machine-read here
human_source: No human performance baseline ('Human' column = human-written jailbreak templates used as an attack baseline). Classifier validated vs. human labels (Llama-2-13B classifier ~93% agreement).
test_access_notes: Validation and test behavior lists released on GitHub (centerforaisafety/HarmBench); rule that attacks/defenses must not be tuned on test behaviors. No hidden labels (judged by released classifier).
curation_notes: Behaviors manually designed by the authors from acceptable-use policies (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Inflection) and filtered for dual-use; standard behaviors modeled after AdvBench and TDC 2023 Red Teaming Track; contextual behaviors add context strings; copyright behaviors judged via hashing.
maintainer: Center for AI Safety (lead; repo centerforaisafety/HarmBench) with UIUC, CMU, UC Berkeley, Microsoft, University of Chicago co-authors
official_leaderboard: no (results in paper and harmbench.org; no submission leaderboard)
lineage: Parents: AdvBench (Zou et al., Jul 2023), TDC 2023 Red Teaming Track. Versions: initial release 2024-02-06 -> HarmBench 1.0 (2024-02-26: precomputed test cases, adversarial-training code). No official successor.
known_contamination_or_defects: No formal label/behavior audit found. Behaviors and precomputed test cases are public, so defenses can be tuned toward them; classifier-based judging (~93% agreement with humans per paper) adds noise.
notes: Dual-purpose benchmark (attacks and defenses); no single canonical model score. 18 red-teaming methods x 33 targets (24 open, 9 closed) at release. 110 multimodal (image+text) behaviors form a separate track; modality recorded as text for the main track. Score here is derived (average of reported per-attack ASRs) - recompute if a different convention is needed. Surprising: at release Claude 2/2.1 were already near-floor (<=4.1% ASR for every attack).

canonical_name: OlympiadBench: Olympiad-level bilingual multimodal scientific benchmark
metric: accuracy (micro-averaged over automatically scorable open-ended problems; numeric/expression/equation/interval/tuple answers checked with SymPy-based pipeline); theorem-proving problems excluded
n_items_source: arXiv v1 (21 Feb 2024): 8,952 problems (6,524 math / 2,428 physics; 7,254 open-ended + 1,698 theorem-proving; 57% with images). Experiments run on auto-scorable open-ended problems (7,254 = upper bound; exact evaluated count not stated). v2/ACL 2024 (6 Jun 2024): 8,476 problems (6,728 open-ended) after deduplication. De-facto LLM math evals use the English text-only math competition subset OE_TO_maths_en_COMP (674 rows on HF; usually cited as 675).
score_at_release_setting: zero-shot, micro-average over all evaluated problems (math 20.35, physics 11.28). Others: Qwen-VL-Max 10.31, Gemini-Pro-Vision 4.38, LLaVA-NeXT-34B 3.60, Yi-VL-34B 3.37. Text-only problems: GPT-4 29.50, GPT-4V 29.24, DeepSeekMath-7B-RL 18.73. v2 (Jun 2024) restated GPT-4V as 17.97 overall / 10.74 physics.
human_source: No human baseline reported
test_access_notes: Full dataset with answers and expert step-by-step solutions released (GitHub OpenBMB/OlympiadBench; HF Hothan/OlympiadBench). No hidden split.
curation_notes: International olympiads (IMO, IPhO, etc.), regional/national Chinese math & physics competitions and Gaokao (incl. mock) problems, 1984-2023; converted from official PDFs to markdown; bilingual (EN/ZH).
maintainer: Tsinghua University (THUNLP / OpenBMB) and collaborators
official_leaderboard: yes (static leaderboard tables in GitHub README: https://github.com/OpenBMB/OlympiadBench)
lineage: No parent. v1 (Feb 2024, 8,952 problems) -> v2 / ACL 2024 (Jun 2024, 8,476 problems, deduplicated; HF upload 2024-07-17). No official successor.
known_contamination_or_defects: Problems come from public competitions (1984-2023) whose solutions are online; authors' only leakage mitigation was sourcing from official PDFs. v2 removed ~476 problems via embedding-based deduplication. No formal contamination audit found.
notes: GitHub release 2024-02-16; arXiv v1 2024-02-21. Headline number in v1 vs v2 differs (17.23 vs 17.97) because the dataset changed.

canonical_name: AIME 2024 (American Invitational Mathematics Examination 2024, AIME I + AIME II)
metric: accuracy (% of problems with the exact integer answer 000-999); LLM reports usually average pass@1 over several samples
n_items_source: AIME I (held 31 Jan-1 Feb 2024) and AIME II (7 Feb 2024), 15 problems each (AoPS wiki exam pages)
score_at_release_setting: No frontier-model AIME 2024 result published in Feb-Mar 2024 was found. Earliest prominent frontier report found: OpenAI 'Learning to reason with LLMs' (12 Sep 2024): GPT-4o 'solved on average 12% (1.8/15)' (outside the window; not recorded as score_at_release).
score_at_release_source: Searched web/news; none found for Feb-Mar 2024
human_source: AoPS wiki 'AMC historical results': AIME I 2024 mean 5.89/15 (39.3%), median 5; AIME II 2024 mean 5.45/15 (36.3%), median 5. 37.8 = unweighted mean of the two exam means (derived). Contestants are AMC 10/12 qualifiers (top few % of AMC takers).
test_access_notes: Problems and official answers public since the exam dates (AoPS wiki, MAA); community datasets on Hugging Face.
curation_notes: Official MAA competition problems written by the AIME problem committee.
maintainer: Mathematical Association of America (exam author); no official AI-benchmark maintainer (community datasets; third-party trackers such as MathArena, Vals.ai)
lineage: Annual series: earlier AIME years (1983-2023) -> AIME 2024 -> AIME 2025 (Feb 2025) -> AIME 2026 (Feb 2026); MathArena (2025) evaluates fresh competitions to avoid contamination.
known_contamination_or_defects: MathArena (arXiv 2505.23281): 'the popular AIME 2024 dataset is significantly contaminated by most leading LLMs'; most models score 10-20% above their expected human-aligned level; QwQ-Preview-32B ~60% above ('extreme contamination').
notes: Human statistics from AoPS wiki (secondary, compiled from MAA reports). A few AIME problems reference figures; LLM versions are text-only. Small n (30) => one problem = 3.33 points.

canonical_name: Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) V1
metric: accuracy (% correct function calls; AST-based matching against possible answers + executable checks), 'Overall Acc' aggregated across 9 categories
n_items_source: Launch blog (27 Feb 2024): 2k question-function-answer pairs = 1,680 Python + 100 Java + 50 JavaScript + 70 REST API + 100 SQL. Leaderboard's 9 scored categories cover 1,700 (AST simple 550 / multiple 200 / parallel 200 / parallel-multiple 200; exec simple 170 / multiple 50 / parallel 50 / parallel-multiple 40; relevance 240 - counts consistent with launch-day per-category accuracies); SQL excluded from the overall score.
score_at_release_setting: Launch-day leaderboard (27 Feb 2024), overall accuracy; all models evaluated by the BFCL team. Next: GPT-4-1106-Preview 83.55, Gorilla OpenFunctions-v2 83.55, GPT-3.5-Turbo 81.63, Mistral-medium 79.46, Claude-2.1 75.78 (16 models listed).
score_at_release_source: leaderboard.html at gh-pages commit 9af2a7c (2024-02-27) of github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla (git history read directly)
human_source: No human baseline
test_access_notes: Questions, function docs and possible answers released (GitHub ShishirPatil/gorilla; HF gorilla-llm/Berkeley-Function-Calling-Leaderboard). Leaderboard scores computed by maintainers (models added by the BFCL team / PRs).
curation_notes: Function docs 'scraped and generated from different sources of websites' across 40 sub-domains; executable functions manually written (inspired by free REST endpoints); REST category uses real GET APIs; relevance-detection items designed by authors. Extends the earlier 100-item Gorilla OpenFunctions eval set.
maintainer: UC Berkeley Gorilla LLM team (Sky Computing Lab; Shishir Patil, Ion Stoica, Joseph Gonzalez et al.)
lineage: Gorilla/APIBench (May 2023) and OpenFunctions eval (100 items) -> BFCL V1 (27 Feb 2024) -> V2 'Live' user-contributed prompts (19 Aug 2024) -> V3 multi-turn, state-based eval (19 Sep 2024) -> V4 agentic: web search, memory, format sensitivity (17 Jul 2025); paper at ICML 2025 (openreview.net/forum?id=2GmDdhBdDk).
known_contamination_or_defects: Frequent dataset/ground-truth fixes in BFCL CHANGELOG: e.g., 8 Mar 2024 clerical error in exec-simple; 3 Apr 2024 possible-answer fixes + string standardization; 9 Apr 2024 prompt/function-doc fixes; 2 May 2024 AST-simple answer fixes; 6 Jul 2024 AST possible answers (14 parallel, 25 parallel-multiple entries); 22 Nov 2024 55 entries with illegal Python parameter names; many later ground-truth fixes. Databricks (16 Aug 2024) noted several BFCL categories are 'far too easy' and model-specific parsing complicates comparison. Data fully public (contamination risk for fine-tuned tool-use models).
notes: Overall-accuracy formula changed over versions (e.g., 5 Mar 2024 patch to overall column; V4 reweighting), so later scores are not directly comparable with the launch 83.80. Format: function-call outputs checked by AST matching and by execution (code-execution-like).

canonical_name: InfiniteBench (∞Bench): Extending Long Context Evaluation Beyond 100K Tokens
metric: per-task score: accuracy for 9 tasks (retrieval, MC, dialogue, code, math); ROUGE F1 for En.QA/Zh.QA; ROUGE-Lsum for En.Sum; overall = unweighted mean of the 12 task scores
n_items_source: arXiv 2402.13718v1: 12 tasks - Retrieve.PassKey 590, Retrieve.Number 590, Retrieve.KV 500, En.Sum 103, En.QA 351, En.MC 229, Zh.QA 189, En.Dia 200, Code.Debug 394, Code.Run 400, Math.Calc 50, Math.Find 350 (total 3,946); average input ~200K tokens; English + Chinese
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 (128K-context version; exact API snapshot not stated in paper)
score_at_release_setting: Unweighted average over 12 tasks (truncation to model context window). Others: Claude 2 37.06, Kimi-Chat 34.73, YaRN-Mistral-7B 19.96. GPT-4 per task: PassKey 100, Number 100, KV 89.00, En.Sum 14.73, En.QA 22.22, En.MC 67.25, En.Dia 8.50, Zh.QA 23.06, Code.Debug 39.59, Code.Run 23.25, Math.Calc 0.01, Math.Find 60.00
human_source: No human baseline (annotation done by the authors with peer quality checks)
test_access_notes: All examples and answers released (GitHub OpenBMB/InfiniteBench; HF xinrongzhang2022/InfiniteBench).
curation_notes: Human-annotated tasks (novel QA/MC/summarization, Zh.QA, Code.Debug, En.Dia) by the authors + synthetic tasks (retrieval passkey/number/KV, Math.Calc, Math.Find, Code.Run). Key-entity replacement (character names) in novels to reduce memorization.
maintainer: Tsinghua University (THUNLP / OpenBMB; Xinrong Zhang, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun et al.)
official_leaderboard: no (results tables in paper/GitHub README only)
lineage: No direct parent (contemporaries: LongBench, L-Eval, needle-in-a-haystack). No official successor version.
known_contamination_or_defects: No formal audit found. Mitigation: key-entity replacement in novel-based tasks. Mixed metric (ROUGE for summarization) and near-zero Math.Calc limit interpretability.
notes: v1 submitted 21 Feb 2024 (ACL 2024). Format mixed (multiple-choice, short answers, free-text QA/summaries scored by ROUGE). Inputs longer than a model's window are truncated by removing the middle. GitHub README (github.com/OpenBMB/InfiniteBench) shows slightly different GPT-4 task values than paper v1 (e.g., En.QA 22.44, Zh.QA 25.96, Code.Debug 37.06).

canonical_name: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of LLMs for Code
metric: pass@1 (fraction of problems whose generated program passes all hidden/public tests; estimated from 10 samples, T=0.2, top_p 0.95)
n_items_source: arXiv v1 (12 Mar 2024): 400 code-generation problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces released May 2023-Feb 2024 (release_v1 = 400 problems May 2023-Mar 2024 per README). Main tables restricted to problems released since Sep 2023 (paper: 238 problems). Other scenarios: code execution 479 samples from 85 problems; test-output prediction 442 instances from 181 LeetCode problems; self-repair uses the code-generation problems.
score_at_release_setting: Code generation, pass@1, problems released since Sep 2023 (Easy 81.9 / Medium 24.5 / Hard 1.1). Next: Claude-3-Opus 32.5, GPT-4-0613 32.2, Mistral-Large 24.2, Claude-3-Sonnet 24.2, Claude-2 23.3, DeepSeek-Coder-33B-Instruct 21.6.
human_source: No human baseline
test_access_notes: Problems and tests public (HF livecodebench/code_generation(_lite)); contamination controlled by evaluating only on problems released after a model's training cutoff; new problems added continuously (release_v1..v6).
curation_notes: Scraped from weekly contests on LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces with release dates; tests from platform/generated; difficulty labels from platforms.
maintainer: UC Berkeley, MIT, Cornell (Naman Jain, King Han, Alex Gu, Ion Stoica, Armando Solar-Lezama, Koushik Sen et al.)
lineage: Rolling releases: release_v1 (May 2023-Mar 2024, 400) -> v2 (to May 2024, 511) -> v3 (to Jul 2024, 612) -> v4 (to Sep 2024, 713) -> v5 (to Jan 2025, 880) -> v6 (to Apr 2025, 1055); code_generation_lite (pruned tests). Related successor: LiveCodeBench Pro (2025, separate team incl. olympiad medalists).
known_contamination_or_defects: Official ERRATA.md (github.com/LiveCodeBench/LiveCodeBench/blob/main/ERRATA.md): ~11 problems accept multiple valid outputs but are graded against one; 2 interactive problems unsolvable by the harness; 4 problems with erroneous test cases. Paper itself documents contamination of older problems: DeepSeek-Coder-33B-Instruct falls from ~60 pass@1 on May-2023 LeetCode problems to ~0 on Sep-2023 problems ('stark drop after Aug. 2023').
notes: Rolling benchmark: 'score' depends on the chosen time window; later reports usually cite a specific window (e.g., v5/v6 windows).

canonical_name: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
metric: success rate (% of tasks completed, judged by task-specific execution-based evaluation scripts; 134 unique evaluation functions)
n_items_source: arXiv v1: 369 Ubuntu tasks (268 single-app, 101 multi-app workflow; 30 infeasible; 84 adapted from prior benchmarks) + 43 Windows tasks reported separately
score_at_release_setting: Overall success rate, a11y-tree observation. Best by setting: Screenshot only - Gemini-ProV 5.80 (GPT-4V 5.26, Claude-3-Opus 2.42); Screenshot+a11y tree - GPT-4V 12.17; Set-of-Mark - GPT-4V 11.77. (Screenshot-only later became the headline 'computer-use' setting.)
n_annotators: not stated (computer-science college students with basic software skills, unseen tasks)
human_source: arXiv v1: human success 72.36% overall (OS 75.00, Office 71.79, Daily 70.51, Professional 73.47, Workflow 73.27); median completion time 111.94 s

canonical_name: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Free LLM Benchmark

n_items_source: arXiv 2406.19314v1: 960 questions, 18 tasks, 6 categories (math, coding, reasoning, data analysis, language, instruction following)
score_at_release_setting: Overall LiveBench score, zero-shot, single run, temperature 0 per paper protocol; next: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 55.0, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 53.0
human_source: No human baseline
test_access_notes: v1: 'We release all questions, code, and model answers'; questions refreshed/added roughly monthly from recent sources (recent math competitions, arXiv papers, news articles, IMDb/Wikipedia plots, LiveCodeBench). Later policy: newest release questions withheld from Hugging Face (README: current 2025-04-25 release not fully public; most recent fully public set 2024-11-25).
curation_notes: Questions derived from recent information sources (math competitions e.g. AMC/AIME/USAMO/IMO, arXiv abstracts, Guardian articles, Kaggle/Socrata tables, LiveCodeBench problems) plus harder/templated versions of BBH, IFEval-style and procedurally generated puzzles (Zebra, Web of Lies).
maintainer: Abacus.AI with NYU, NVIDIA, UMD, USC (Colin White, Samuel Dooley, Micah Goldblum, Yann LeCun et al.)
lineage: Rolling releases (changelog): initial Jun 2024 -> 2024-07-26 (new coding Qs, spatial reasoning) -> 2024-08-31 (math refresh: IMO/USAMO 2024) -> 2024-11-25 (harder IF/Connections/Zebra) -> 2025-04-02 -> 2025-04-25 (new real-world-library coding Qs) -> 2025-05-30 (agentic coding category) -> 2025-11-25 (refresh vs saturation/contamination) -> 2025-12-23, 2026-01-08 (new tasks).

canonical_name: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
metric: pass^1 = average reward (task success: final database state matches annotated goal state and required information conveyed), plus pass^k reliability (all k i.i.d. trials succeed)
n_items_source: arXiv v1: τ-retail 115 tasks (500 users, 50 products, 1,000 orders) + τ-airline 50 tasks (500 users, 300 flights, 2,000 reservations)
score_at_release_setting: Average of the two domains (paper's 'avg', weighted by domain): retail 61.2, airline 35.2; user simulator gpt-4-0613. Others (retail/airline): gpt-4-turbo 57.7/32.4, gpt-4-32k 56.5/33.0, claude-3-opus 44.2/34.7, mistral-large 30.7/22.4, gemini-1.5-pro 21.7/14.0. gpt-4o pass^8 on retail ~25%.
human_source: No human baseline
test_access_notes: Tasks, databases, policies and ground-truth action sequences released on GitHub (sierra-research/tau-bench); original repo tasks are no longer updated (README points to τ³-bench for fixed tasks).
curation_notes: Manual design of schemas, APIs and domain policies; LM-assisted generation of database entries; tasks/user instructions written and iteratively verified by the authors (e.g., >40 gpt-4-turbo trials per retail task during annotation).
maintainer: Sierra (Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan)
official_leaderboard: no dedicated leaderboard at release (results in paper/README); later web leaderboard https://taubench.com (τ²/τ³-bench)
lineage: τ-bench (Jun 2024; retail, airline) -> τ²-bench (9 Jun 2025, arXiv 2506.07982; dual-control telecom domain, revised airline/retail) -> τ³-bench (v1.0.0, 18 Mar 2026; voice evaluation, banking_knowledge domain with 97 tasks).
known_contamination_or_defects: τ³-bench release notes (github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/releases, 18 Mar 2026): 27 airline tasks corrected and 26 retail tasks fixed for invalid actions/ambiguous instructions (i.e., ~1 in 4 original tasks had issues). Original τ-bench README: 'The tasks in this repo are not updated' - use τ³-bench for fixed tasks. Results depend on the LLM user simulator (stochastic).
notes: arXiv v1 17 Jun 2024. Later reports usually cite retail and airline separately (often with different user simulators), so compare per domain.

canonical_name: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark
metric: accuracy (up to 10-option multiple choice), 5-shot chain-of-thought
n_items_source: arXiv v1: 12,032 test questions in 14 disciplines (from original MMLU 6,810; STEM websites 4,083; TheoremQA 598; SciBench 541); plus a small validation/few-shot split
score_at_release_setting: 5-shot CoT, overall accuracy. Next: Gemini-1.5-Pro 69.0, Claude-3-Opus 68.5, GPT-4-Turbo 63.7, Llama-3-70B-Instruct 56.2.
human_source: No human baseline
test_access_notes: Full test set with answers on Hugging Face (TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro).
curation_notes: Original MMLU questions filtered (5,886 'too easy' questions removed: answered correctly by >4 of 8 small models) + questions from STEM websites, TheoremQA and SciBench; options expanded from 4 to 10 with GPT-4-Turbo-generated distractors; two-phase expert review (with Gemini-1.5-Pro flagging false-negative options).
maintainer: TIGER-Lab, University of Waterloo (Yubo Wang, Wenhu Chen et al.) with collaborators
lineage: MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2020) -> MMLU-Pro (Jun 2024; NeurIPS 2024 D&B). Third-party derivatives: MMLU-Pro+ (Oct 2024), MMLU-ProX (multilingual, 2025); related clean-up of MMLU: MMLU-Redux (Jun 2024).
known_contamination_or_defects: Paper's expert review found in source pools: incorrect answers (MMLU 350, STEM web 483, SciBench 11), false-negative options (MMLU 1,953) and bad questions (MMLU 385, STEM web 862) before release. Post-release: HF discussion #22 (Sep 2024) - only ~83% of test questions actually have 10 options (3-10 after filtering), acknowledged by maintainers; HF discussion #36 (25 Oct 2025) - 39 'health' questions recategorized, 1 wrong answer fixed, near-duplicates and time-sensitive questions documented.
notes: arXiv v1 3 Jun 2024. Answer extraction via regex with fallback; prompt/extraction differences cause cross-lab variance.

canonical_name: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
metric: three rates: benign utility (% of 97 user tasks solved without attack), utility under attack (% of security cases where user task solved and no attacker side-effect), targeted attack success rate (ASR, % of cases where attacker goal achieved; lower = more secure). Headline here: utility under attack
n_items_source: arXiv v1: 4 environments (Workspace, Slack, Travel, Banking), 97 user tasks, 27 injection tasks, 629 security test cases (user x injection task pairs), 74 tools
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 Turbo (utility under attack, 'important message' attack, no defense)
score_at_release_setting: Table 3 (95% CI): GPT-4 Turbo benign 58.98 / under attack 51.67 / ASR 31.96; Claude 3 Opus 64.39 / 49.60 / 12.89; GPT-4o 69.00 (best benign utility) / 44.99 / 53.10; Command-R+ lowest ASR 0.95 (benign 27.78). Defense: tool filter cut GPT-4o targeted ASR to 7.5%.
human_source: No human baseline
test_access_notes: Environments, tasks, injection tasks and checkers open-source (github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo; pip package); results explorer with traces at agentdojo.spylab.ai/results.
curation_notes: User and injection tasks hand-designed by the authors; environment dummy data written manually and with GPT-4 / Claude 3 Opus assistance, then manually inspected. Tasks checked by deterministic state/utility functions.
maintainer: ETH Zurich SPY Lab (Edoardo Debenedetti, Florian Tramèr et al.) with Invariant Labs; later contributions from UK AISI
lineage: AgentDojo benchmark v1 (Jun 2024; NeurIPS 2024 D&B) -> v1.1 -> v1.2 (task/injection updates and fixes, incl. UK AISI contributions) -> v1.2.1 / v1.2.2 tasks (2025). Related earlier work: InjecAgent, BIPIA.
known_contamination_or_defects: Package changelog documents task-checker bugs: e.g., v0.1.15 fixed imprecise security checks for Workspace injection tasks 4 and 5; v0.1.21 'Fix several bugs in tasks verifications'; v0.1.30 'Fix some issues in Benchmark v1.2'. Website results (re-run, later benchmark versions) differ from paper v1 (e.g., GPT-4o utility 69.07 / under attack 50.08 / ASR 47.69).
notes: arXiv v1 19 Jun 2024. Security benchmark with no single canonical score; utility-under-attack chosen as headline because it rewards both capability and robustness (benign utility alone: GPT-4o 69.00; ASR alone: lower is better). Note ±3.6-3.9 CIs.

canonical_name: OfficeBench: Benchmarking Language Agents across Multiple Applications for Office Automation

curation_notes: Tasks written/annotated by the authors (UCSD, UCLA, AI2) around realistic office workflows across applications, each with a customized evaluation function.
maintainer: UC San Diego, UCLA and Allen Institute for AI (Zilong Wang, Jingbo Shang et al.)

canonical_name: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models
metric: unguided success rate (% of 40 CTF tasks where the agent captures the flag); also subtask-guided success and subtask performance
n_items_source: arXiv v1: 40 professional CTF tasks from 4 competitions (HackTheBox 17, SekaiCTF 12, Glacier 9, HKCert 2); 17 tasks have subtasks
score_at_release_setting: Unguided, single attempt with the paper's agent scaffold (reflection/plan/thought/log/action, bash in Kali Linux container, limited iterations). GPT-4o 12.5, Claude 3 Opus 10.0. Subtask-guided (17 tasks): GPT-4o 29.4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 23.5. Subtask performance: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 48.5. Hardest task solved unguided had first-solve-time 11 min.
human_source: No human success-rate baseline; human 'first solve time' (FST) of the fastest competition team is used as a difficulty measure (2 min to 24 h 54 min).
test_access_notes: Task containers, flags and subtasks are public on GitHub (andyzorigin/cybench); public CTF writeups exist for the original competitions.
curation_notes: Tasks taken from recent professional-level CTF competitions (2022-2024) and packaged with environments; subtasks newly written by the authors.
maintainer: Stanford University (Andy K. Zhang, Neil Perry, Dan Boneh, Percy Liang et al.)
lineage: No direct parent (packages tasks from public CTF competitions); widely used in lab system cards and government AI-safety-institute pre-deployment tests; no official successor version found.
known_contamination_or_defects: Paper notes contamination risk: nearly half of tasks released after Dec 2023 but Claude 3.5 Sonnet's Apr 2024 cutoff may overlap some tasks; competition writeups are public. No label/task-error audit found.
notes: arXiv v1 15 Aug 2024 (ICLR 2025). Very small n (40): one task = 2.5 points.

canonical_name: SWE-bench Verified (500-task human-validated subset of SWE-bench test)

n_items_source: OpenAI post (13 Aug 2024): 1,699 random SWE-bench test samples annotated 3x each by 93 Python developers; 68.3% filtered (underspecified issue, unfair tests, other); 500 verified samples released (196 '<15 min' easy, 45 '>1 h' hard)
score_at_release_setting: Top entry on the official SWE-bench Verified leaderboard at launch (swebench.com data.json, commit of 13 Aug 2024; 14 entries, all re-scored existing submissions): next AutoCodeRover v20240620 + GPT-4o 38.4, Factory Code Droid 37.0, SWE-agent + Claude 3.5 Sonnet 33.6, AppMap Navie + GPT-4o 26.2. OpenAI's own launch-post best: GPT-4o + Agentless 33.2 (vs 16% on full SWE-bench).
score_at_release_source: github.com/SWE-bench/swe-bench.github.io template/data.json at commit ab67925 (2024-08-13, 'Update leaderboard'; Verified board added 2024-08-11) - git history read directly; OpenAI launch post
n_annotators: 93 professional Python developers (validation of tasks, not a performance baseline)
human_source: No human solve-rate baseline; annotators estimated fix time (difficulty buckets).
test_access_notes: Issues, repos, gold patches and tests public (HF princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified); leaderboard entries submitted with predictions/logs and verified by SWE-bench maintainers.

maintainer: OpenAI (Preparedness) created the subset with the SWE-bench authors (Princeton/Stanford); leaderboard maintained by the SWE-bench team
lineage: SWE-bench (Oct 2023, 2,294 tasks) -> SWE-bench Lite (Mar 2024, 300) -> SWE-bench Verified (Aug 2024, 500) -> SWE-bench Multimodal (Oct 2024), SWE-bench Multilingual (2025); external successors e.g. SWE-bench Pro (Scale AI, Sep 2025), which OpenAI recommended in Feb 2026.
known_contamination_or_defects: OpenAI 'Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities' (23 Feb 2026): audit of 138 problems o3 failed inconsistently found 59.4% with material test-design issues (35.5% overly strict tests, 18.8% tests of undocumented functionality, 5.1% other); frontier models (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Flash) reproduced gold patches/verbatim details => contamination; OpenAI stopped reporting it. SWE-bench issue #465 (Sep 2025): agents could read future git history (commits/reflogs/tags) in task containers; exploited by Claude 4 Sonnet/Opus, Qwen3-Coder, GPT-5 (~1.2% impact for Opus); fixed with new Docker images.
notes: Launch-day leaderboard verified from the website repo history (13 Aug 2024). Scaffold-dependent metric (agent+model systems). Current experiments repo shows slightly different values for some old entries (e.g., SWE-agent + Claude 3 Opus 15.8 now vs 18.2 at launch).

canonical_name: MMMU-Pro: A More Robust Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding Benchmark
metric: accuracy; overall MMMU-Pro score = mean of Standard (10 options) and Vision (question embedded in screenshot/photo) settings
n_items_source: arXiv v1: 1,730 questions, each in Standard-10-option and Vision form (3,460 total); built from MMMU by (1) removing questions answerable by text-only LLMs (>=3 of 4 open LLMs correct), sampling 1,800, (2) expanding options to 10 with GPT-4o + human experts (70 more removed), (3) vision-only screenshots/photos
score_at_release_setting: Overall = mean(Standard-10 54.0, Vision 49.7); best of direct vs CoT prompting per model. Standard-4-options 64.7. Random choice 12.6.

test_access_notes: All 1,730 questions with answers on Hugging Face (MMMU/MMMU_Pro: standard-10, standard-4, vision configs).
curation_notes: Filtered subset of MMMU (exam/textbook questions) + augmented distractors (GPT-4o-assisted, human-reviewed) + human-captured screenshots/photos for the vision setting.
maintainer: MMMU Team (Xiang Yue, Wenhu Chen, Graham Neubig et al.; multi-institution academic team - v1 lists only 'MMMU Team')
